import pandas as pd

# Load source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the numerical index column
source0_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_83/training_0.csv"
source1_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_83/training_1.csv"

df0 = pd.read_csv(source0_path, index_col=0)
df1 = pd.read_csv(source1_path, index_col=0)

# Operation 1: JOIN Source4_83_0 and Source4_83_1 on "city"
# Both have a "city" column, join on that
df_joined = pd.merge(df0, df1, on="city", how="inner")

# Operation 2: group_by ["Source4_83_1.city", "Source4_83_1.type"]
# aggregations: COUNT(Source4_83_0.ride_id) as driver_count, AVG(Source4_83_0.fare) as average_fare
# Note: "city" and "type" come from Source4_83_1 after join, so columns are "city" and "type"
grouped = df_joined.groupby(["city", "type"], as_index=False).agg(
    driver_count=pd.NamedAgg(column="ride_id", aggfunc="count"),
    average_fare=pd.NamedAgg(column="fare", aggfunc="mean"),
)

# Reorder columns to match target schema: ['city', 'driver_count', 'type', 'average_fare']
# Target schema order is: city (string), driver_count (int), type (string), average_fare (float)
# Ensure driver_count is int and average_fare is float
grouped["driver_count"] = grouped["driver_count"].astype(int)
grouped["average_fare"] = grouped["average_fare"].astype(float)

# Save the result to the target path
target_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_83/target_multisource.csv"
grouped.to_csv(target_path, index=False)
